decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard-Venusaur to immediately activate Drought+Chlorophyll sun engine for Solar Beam speed advantage. Back pair Scizor and Excadrill cover Fairy threats (Bullet Punch) and Electric/Camerupt (Mold Breaker Rock Slide). Toxapex and Weavile remain on bench as flexible switch-in answers.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leans Fairy/special-heavy (Mega Floette, Mega Camerupt). Sun team core: Mega Charizard Y Drought fuels Venusaur Chlorophyll SolarBeam. Scizor Technician Bullet Punch = mandatory Fairy check. Excadrill Mold Breaker punishes Electric types and Camerupt. Toxapex 4x SE Surf walls Mega Camerupt Fire/Ground, spreads Toxic. Weavile Ice Shard priority handles fast threats and revenge-kills. Watch for Farigiraf Trick Room; Weavile/Scizor speed tiers are our answer. Opponent has Mega Camerupt (Sheer Force) and Mega Floette—keep Toxapex healthy for Surf chip.

decisions.rationale: Lead Farigiraf + Heliolisk pressures the expected Charizard-Y sun mode: Armor Tail denies priority disruption and Helping Hand Thunderbolt threatens Charizard. Mega Camerupt provides the Trick Room endgame against Venusaur, Scizor, Excadrill, and Toxapex, while Tauros adds Intimidate and Rock Slide pressure.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 preview plan: lead Farigiraf/Heliolisk into the likely Charizard-Y sun composition. Preserve Farigiraf to establish Trick Room for Mega Camerupt when advantageous. Tauros is the fourth for Intimidate, Rock Slide Charizard pressure, and flexible physical cleanup. Opponent revealed roster: Charizard-Y, Venusaur, Scizor, Excadrill, Toxapex, Weavile.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Farigiraf to eliminate the Trick Room threat before it activates (Trick Room has -7 priority so our moves land first). Mega Evolving Charizard Y sets Drought, enabling Venusaur's Solar Beam to fire in one turn under sun. Both moves are neutral on Normal/Psychic but Farigiraw's low defenses make a KO likely, removing Psychic Noise (2x vs Venusaur) and Trick Room in one turn.

Scizor Technician Bullet Punch = mandatory Fairy check. Excadrill Mold Breaker punishes Electric types and Camerupt. Toxapex 4x SE Surf walls Mega Camerupt Fire/Ground, spreads Toxic. Turn 1: opened with Mega Charizard Y Drought + Venusaur Solar Beam double-targeting Farigiraf to remove Trick Room threat and establish sun.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill's Mold Breaker Earthquake OHKOs Heliolisk (87%, Focus Sash broken), removing their Electric threat and creating a 2v1. Speed 154 outruns Farigiraf's max 100, deterring Trick Room. Venusaur passes to let charging Solar Beam fire.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leans Fairy/special-heavy (Mega Floette, Mega Camerupt). Sun core: Mega Charizard Y Drought fuels Venusaur Chlorophyll SolarBeam. Scizor Technician Bullet Punch is mandatory Fairy check. Excadrill Mold Breaker punishes Electric types and Camerupt. Toxapex 4x SE Surf walls Mega Camerupt, spreads Toxic. Weavile Ice Shard handles fast threats. Watch Farigiraf Trick Room. Heliolisk Focus Sash consumed. Farigiraf at 48% after Helping Hand. Prioritize removing remaining foes efficiently.

decisions.rationale: Helping Hand Thunderbolt guarantees a KO on Mega Charizard Y if it attacks, immediately removing the sun engine and strongest Trick Room denial. It also forces Charizard into Protect rather than allowing it to freely double Farigiraf; Farigiraf remains healthy to establish Trick Room on a later turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 opponent roster revealed: Charizard-Y, Venusaur, plus two of Scizor, Excadrill, Toxapex, Weavile. Charizard-Y brings Drought; Venusaur has Chlorophyll but no Sleep Powder, carrying Sludge Bomb/Solar Beam/Giga Drain/Protect. Heliolisk is faster than Charizard before Trick Room and Solar Power + Helping Hand Thunderbolt is a guaranteed OHKO on Mega Charizard-Y in sun. Preserve Farigiraf where possible for Trick Room and Mega Camerupt endgame; Armor Tail blocks priority. Tauros offers Intimidate and Rock Slide pressure.

decisions.rationale: Solar Beam finishes charging in sun; target Farigiraf (48%) to KO the Trick Room user and Psychic Noise threat. Excadrill adds Iron Head on Farigiraf to secure the KO. Excadrill is immune to Heliolisk's Electric moves, so any response from Heliolisk is harmless.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leans Fairy/special-heavy (Mega Floette, Mega Camerupt). Sun core: Mega Charizard Y Drought fuels Venusaur Chlorophyll SolarBeam. Scizor Technician Bullet Punch is mandatory Fairy check. Excadrill Mold Breaker punishes Electric types and Camerupt. Toxapex 4x SE Surf walls Mega Camerupt, spreads Toxic. Weavile Ice Shard handles fast threats. Watch Farigiraf Trick Room. Heliolisk Focus Sash consumed. Prioritize removing remaining foes efficiently.

decisions.rationale: Protect blocks the charged Solar Beam while Volt Switch chips Venusaur and brings in Tauros with Intimidate before Excadrill can attack, preserving Farigiraf and keeping Heliolisk available for later.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 opponent’s fourth is Excadrill (Mold Breaker, Focus Sash, Jolly); opponent did not bring Scizor, Toxapex, or Weavile. Venusaur’s revealed set lacks Sleep Powder and is Timid Chlorophyll with Miracle Seed. Prioritize removing Venusaur before committing Mega Camerupt, since sun enables immediate Solar Beam. Tauros’s Intimidate is valuable into Excadrill; preserve Farigiraf if possible to establish Trick Room for Mega Camerupt.

decisions.rationale: Switch Heliolisk to Tauros: Intimidate immediately weakens Excadrill, while Tauros takes the pending Solar Beam far better than Camerupt. Preserve Camerupt for a later Trick Room turn after Venusaur is removed.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 opponent’s fourth is Excadrill (Mold Breaker, Focus Sash, Jolly); opponent did not bring Scizor, Toxapex, or Weavile. Venusaur is Timid Chlorophyll with Miracle Seed and has Sludge Bomb, Solar Beam, Giga Drain, Protect; no Sleep Powder revealed. Charizard-Mega-Y is removed. Prioritize removing Venusaur before committing Mega Camerupt, since sun enables immediate Solar Beam. Tauros’s Intimidate is valuable into Excadrill; preserve Farigiraf if possible to establish Trick Room for Mega Camerupt.

decisions.rationale: Target Farigiraf with both attacks to eliminate the weakened Trick Room threat at 48% HP. Excadrill's Iron Head pressures it physically while Venusaur's fully-charged Solar Beam adds heavy special damage in sun. Removing Farigiraf early prevents Trick Room reversal and reduces Psychic Noise risk to Venusaur.
decisions.notebook: Opponent likely has Mega Floette or Mega Camerupt remaining. Sun core (Mega Charizard Y Drought + Venusaur Chlorophyll) fuels Solar Beam charges. Scizor mandatory Fairy check still in reserve. Excadrill Mold Breaker punishes Electric/Camerupt. Heliolisk Focus Sash gone. Tauros Intimidate already applied to Excadrill. Prioritize Farigiraf elimination before Trick Room sets up.

decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Tauros from Venusaur’s sun-boosted Solar Beam while Farigiraf safely pressures Venusaur with Psychic Noise and prevents recovery. Excadrill’s revealed Iron Head alone cannot remove Farigiraf from its current range, leaving a strong follow-up position to clear Venusaur and then establish Trick Room for Mega Camerupt.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent’s brought four are Mega Charizard Y, Venusaur, and Focus Sash Mold Breaker Jolly Excadrill plus an unrevealed fourth; Scizor, Toxapex, and Weavile were not brought. Venusaur is Timid Chlorophyll with Miracle Seed: Sludge Bomb, Solar Beam, Giga Drain, Protect; no Sleep Powder revealed. Charizard Y is removed. Venusaur’s sun Solar Beam heavily threatens Tauros, while Sludge Bomb and -1 Excadrill Iron Head individually do not immediately KO Farigiraf from mid health. Preserve Tauros where possible; Psychic Noise is valuable to deny Venusaur recovery. Prioritize Venusaur before exposing Mega Camerupt to sun-accelerated Solar Beam, then use Trick Room to enable Camerupt.

decisions.rationale: Use the already-chipped Heliolisk as the replacement into Venusaur’s pending Solar Beam, preserving full-health Camerupt for the endgame once sun pressure is reduced. Tauros has no available action.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Mega Charizard Y, Timid Chlorophyll Miracle Seed Venusaur (Sludge Bomb / Solar Beam / Giga Drain / Protect), and Focus Sash Mold Breaker Jolly Excadrill; fourth remains unrevealed. Charizard Y is removed. Venusaur has shown Solar Beam repeatedly and its sun is a major threat; Solar Beam is neutral into both Camerupt and Heliolisk, with Camerupt’s Solid Rock helping. Excadrill was Intimidated once. Preserve Tauros and Mega Camerupt when possible; remove Excadrill with Tauros Fighting STAB, then manage Venusaur with sun expiry and Camerupt pressure. Farigiraf is gone, so Trick Room is unavailable this game. Heliolisk’s Focus Sash is no longer intact after Solar Power chip.

decisions.rationale: Focus fire Tauros-Paldea-Combat, the biggest physical threat to Excadrill. Venusaur's Solar Beam fires in sun after charging; combined with Excadrill's Iron Head, this maximizes KO chance on Tauros. Even if Tauros Protects, its reduced success rate makes failure likely. Removing Tauros eliminates the 2x Close Combat threat to Excadrill and leaves a manageable Heliolisk.
decisions.notebook: Opponent likely has Mega Floette or Mega Camerupt in reserve. Sun core (Mega Charizard Y Drought + Venusaur Chlorophyll) fuels Solar Beam. Scizor reserved as Fairy check. Heliolisk Focus Sash already consumed. Farigiraf eliminated before Trick Room could set up. Prioritize Tauros removal to protect Excadrill, then pressure Heliolisk with type advantage options.

decisions.rationale: Protect Heliolisk from Venusaur’s immediate sun-boosted Solar Beam pressure while Tauros uses its guaranteed high-power Fighting hit into Excadrill. Close Combat is needed to ensure Focus Sash activation/removal rather than risking Raging Bull damage falling short.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 opponent’s confirmed core: Mega Charizard Y, Timid Chlorophyll Miracle Seed Venusaur (Sludge Bomb / Solar Beam / Giga Drain / Protect), and Jolly Mold Breaker Focus Sash Excadrill (Earthquake / Iron Head / Rock Slide / Protect). Their fourth is unrevealed among Scizor, Toxapex, and Weavile. Venusaur is a major sun attacker and becomes much more manageable once sun ends; Excadrill’s Focus Sash must be accounted for. Preserve Tauros and Mega Camerupt where possible; Camerupt is the key endgame damage source.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Combined Solar Beam + Earthquake almost certainly OHKOs Camerupt (the biggest threat with Mega Eruption that OHKOs both Venusaur and any switch-in). Earthquake also heavily damages Heliolisk. Earthquake's recoil on Venusaur is only ~35%, survivable. Removing Camerupt wins the game.
decisions.notebook: Camerupt is the primary threat—Mega Eruption OHKOs Scizor (4x) and Venusaur (2x). Solar Beam + Earthquake combined deal 95-226% to Camerupt, near-guaranteed OHKO. Earthquake also pressures Heliolisk (54-141% at 75% HP). Earthquake recoil on Venusaur is ~33-38%, leaving it at ~35-41%. After Camerupt removal, Heliolisk is manageable; Scizor remains as Fairy check for potential Mega Floette. Prioritize Camerupt elimination above all.

decisions.rationale: Mega Eruption is the only line that can immediately remove both active foes if Camerupt survives Venusaur’s Solar Beam plus Excadrill’s Earthquake; its damage is a guaranteed KO on Venusaur from 73% and should also erase the 1% Excadrill. Thunderbolt adds Venusaur chip if Camerupt is denied its move.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 opponent’s confirmed core: Mega Charizard Y, Timid Chlorophyll Miracle Seed Venusaur (Sludge Bomb / Solar Beam / Giga Drain / Protect), and Jolly Mold Breaker Focus Sash Excadrill (Earthquake / Iron Head / Rock Slide / Protect). Their fourth is unrevealed among Scizor, Toxapex, and Weavile. Venusaur is a major sun attacker and becomes much more manageable once sun ends; Excadrill’s Focus Sash has been consumed. Mega Camerupt’s huge Special Attack gives Eruption a strong endgame-cleaning role, but Mold Breaker Excadrill can pressure it with Earthquake.

reflections.summary: Excadrill's Focus Sash let it survive Tauros's Close Combat at 1% on Turn 4, then Earthquake on Turn 5 OHKOed both Heliolisk and Camerupt-Mega simultaneously (both super effective), clinching the win. Charizard-Mega-Y was mispositioned—it died turn 1 to Heliolisk's Thunderbolt, a predictable outcome given Heliolisk's SolarPower + Thunderbolt is a hard counter. Scizor was dead weight the entire game. The win hinged on the double-Earthquake coin flip landing favorably.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Charizard-Mega-Y with a Pokemon that handles Heliolisk and isn't 4x/2x weak to opposing threats. Heliolisk's Thunderbolt hard-counters Charizard-Y, and the opponent previewed it. A faster Ground-type or a bulky pivot that discourages Thunderbolt targeting (or can threaten Heliolisk back) would add consistency. Also consider whether Scizor earns its slot—its Fairy check role was irrelevant here and Camerupt doesn't fear Bullet Punch.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's core: Camerupt-Mega (Eruption nuke, 4x Earthquake weak), Heliolisk (SolarPower Thunderbolt, Focus Sash), Farigiraf (Trick Room setter with Helping Hand support—Trick Room unused this game, may deploy in Game 2), Tauros-Paldea-Combat (Intimidate + Close Combat breaker). Floette-Eternal and Liepard (Prankster Taunt/Encore) were benched—expect one or both in Game 2 as anti-meta answers. Camerupt-Mega remains the primary priority target; Solar Beam + Earthquake is the confirmed kill combination. Excadrill with Focus Sash + Mold Breaker + Earthquake is the MVP against this lineup. Opponent's Farigiraf is frail despite Helping Hand recovery.

reflections.summary: Lost because the Charizard Y/Venusaur sun core plus Focus Sash Mold Breaker Excadrill overwhelmed the Heliolisk/Farigiraf lead after Trick Room was never established; Mega Camerupt entered into Solar Beam and Earthquake pressure and could not use its slow-mode payoff.
reflections.adjustment: Rework the preview plan: do not rely on Mega Camerupt unless Trick Room can be established safely against this sun/Excadrill shell; prioritize a fourth that handles Venusaur and Excadrill over Tauros, and use Farigiraf’s Trick Room earlier rather than only supporting Heliolisk’s Charizard knockout.
reflections.notebook: Opponent led Mega Charizard Y + Chlorophyll Miracle Seed Venusaur and repeatedly used Solar Beam under sun. Excadrill is Jolly Mold Breaker Focus Sash with Earthquake, Iron Head, Rock Slide, and Protect; it can bypass standard ability-based counterplay and threatens Mega Camerupt directly. Charizard Y, Venusaur, and Excadrill are confirmed; fourth remains unrevealed among Scizor, Toxapex, and Weavile. Future plan: respect the sun Solar Beam/Earthquake pairing at preview and only select Mega Camerupt with a credible Trick Room route.
